extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance for preparing complete patent drawings in U.S. nonprovisional applications, describing what must be shown, how conventional features may be represented, and procedural requirements for corrected/replacement drawing sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show every feature specified in the claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing in a nonprovisional application must show every feature of the invention specified in the claims. (37 C.F.R. 1.83(a))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any feature recited in the claims should be depicted in the drawings. If a claimed feature is not shown, the examiner will object and require corrected drawing sheets in reply to the Office action to avoid abandonment. If a drawing figure is to be canceled, remove it from the replacement sheet and renumber remaining figures with consistent changes to the brief description of the several views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventional features may be represented by symbols or labeled boxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventional features disclosed in the description and claims, where their detailed illustration is not essential for a proper understanding of the invention, should be illustrated in the drawing in the form of a graphical drawing symbol or a labeled representation (e.g., a labeled rectangular box). (37 C.F.R. 1.83(a))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not omit conventional elements entirely if they are necessary to understand the claimed invention; instead use simplified graphical symbols or labeled representations when detailed illustration is not essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not duplicate tables or sequence listings in the drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables that are included in the specification and sequences that are included in sequence listings should not be duplicated in the drawings. (37 C.F.R. 1.83(a))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid repeating material already set out as tables or in sequence listings within the drawing sheets; include such material only in the appropriate part of the specification or sequence listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show improved portion and necessary old structure for improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: When the invention consists of an improvement on an old machine the drawing must when possible exhibit, in one or more views, the improved portion itself, disconnected from the old structure, and also in another view, so much only of the old structure as will suffice to show the connection of the invention therewith. (37 C.F.R. 1.83(b))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide both a standalone view of the improved part and a view showing how it connects to the preexisting structure so the connection and improvements are clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Any structurally important detail disclosed should be shown
rubrics_metrics.description: Any structural detail that is of sufficient importance to be described should be shown in the drawing. (Ex parte Good, 1911 C.D. 43, 164 OG 739)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a structural detail is described in the specification and is important to understanding or practicing the invention, include it in the drawings rather than omitting it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner will require additional illustration if drawings noncompliant
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the drawings in a nonprovisional application do not comply with the requirements of paragraphs (a) and (b), the examiner shall require such additional illustration within a time period of not less than two months from the date of the sending of a notice thereof. Corrections are subject to the requirements of 37 C.F.R. 1.81(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an examiner objects, the applicant will be given at least two months to submit required illustrations. Corrections must meet the formal requirements (e.g., 1.81(d)) and be submitted as corrected/replacement sheets per 37 C.F.R. 1.121(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrected/replacement drawing sheet submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrected drawing sheets in compliance with 37 C.F.R. 1.121(d) are required in reply to the Office action to avoid abandonment. Any amended replacement drawing sheet should include all of the figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet, even if only one figure is being amended. The figure or figure number of an amended drawing should not be labeled as 'amended.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting replacement sheets: include all figures that were on the prior version of that sheet; do not label figures as 'amended'; if canceling a figure, remove it and renumber remaining figures and update the brief description of the drawings for consistency; additional replacement sheets may be necessary to show renumbering; label each drawing sheet submitted after filing as either 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet' in the top margin (37 C.F.R. 1.121(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: If changes not accepted, examiner will notify and objection not held in abeyance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the changes are not accepted by the examiner, the applicant will be notified and informed of any required corrective action in the next Office action. The objection to the drawings will not be held in abeyance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not expect objections to be deferred; if the examiner rejects submitted corrections the applicant will be told how to proceed in the subsequent Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests to hold drawing objections in abeyance are not allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless applicant is otherwise notified in an Office action, objections to the drawings in a utility or plant application will not be held in abeyance, and a request to hold objections to the drawings in abeyance will not be considered a bona fide attempt to advance the application to final action. See 37 C.F.R. 1.85(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to delay addressing drawing objections by asking the examiner to hold them in abeyance; such requests are not viewed as bona fide attempts to advance prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: If drawings incomplete, supply a full explanation when replying
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply a full explanation, if it is not readily apparent how the drawings are incomplete. (Examiner Note under ¶ 6.22.04)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When responding to an objection that drawings are incomplete, explain clearly why the original drawings were sufficient or provide the additional illustrations requested and annotate what was added so the examiner can readily see the correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: If claimed subject matter not shown, show it or cancel the claim (no new matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawings must show every feature of the invention specified in the claims. Therefore, the [feature] must be shown or the feature(s) canceled from the claim(s). No new matter should be entered. (¶ 6.36, under 37 C.F.R. 1.83(a))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a claimed element is missing from the drawings, the applicant must either add the missing illustration or amend the claims to remove the element; you may not add new matter in the process of correcting drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a marked-up copy with annotations when requested
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 6.27 may be used to require a marked up copy of the amended drawing figure(s) including annotations indicating the changes made in the corrected drawings. (Examiner Note)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the examiner requests it, submit annotated/marked-up figures that clearly indicate what changes were made to facilitate examiner review of the corrected drawings.
